name: Finnian Goodbarrel
tagline: Halfling rogue, with a criminal past
intro: You've lived on the wrong side of Waterdeep's law, and it shows in how you see the city: who's watching, what's worth taking, and which doors stay unlocked.

sections.heading: You know the underworld
sections.because: Criminal background · Thieves' Cant · Expertise in Stealth and Sleight of Hand
sections.lead: Freelancers like you get by on knowing whose turf you're standing on. Working Xanathar turf without permission is a quick way to get hurt.

sections.heading: You know the halfling side of the city
extra: You know of the Shard Shunners, and they may well know of you.
Gnomish is useful when you need a lock understood, or a trinket appraised quietly.

sections.heading: You know some history
extra: With the treasury strained by the curse, **Neverember's stolen gold** isn't just a tavern story anymore. People with real power would very much like to find it.
The city's old **thieves' guild** was destroyed by the Lords long ago. That's why the underworld is a free-for-all today.
You know the major houses by name and reputation. Useful when choosing whose purse not to lift.

sections.heading: You notice things
sections.because: Investigation and Perception proficiency · Alert · a thief's habits (Criminal background)
sections.lead: You also know the routes and shortcuts every working thief learns.
extra: Watch patrols are thinnest where wards meet, and their timing is predictable within a ward.
Dock Ward and Trades Ward rooftops are close enough to cross on foot if you're nimble.
Many cellars connect to the sewers, and some connect to each other in ways no plan shows.

lists.heading: Languages
items: **Thieves' Cant:** you read the sigils and hidden phrases of the trade.
**Common Sign Language:** handy for silent work.

story: *Not written yet. Talk to your DM about where Finnian grew up, who he ran with, and who he owes. This section will grow with your backstory.*

secrets.because: Investigation proficiency. You know people who know things.
extra: The ships were quietly chartered with city coin. Some of the crews haven't come back.
Smugglers and fences have noticed buyers paying silly money for anything out of Chult: charms, idols, maps, "cures."
The few people in the know keep their mouths shut, because a secret that size is worth something.
